Google is completely turning off Search for K-12 schools that reject its AI features.

Here is what software engineers and AI developers should track from today's developments across model verification, search access, and hardware engineering workflows.

🔐 Anthropic released FlashProve, an Apache 2.0 open-source zkSNARK prototype. The tool generates 19 MB cryptographic proofs that verify a reply came from a committed model without revealing its underlying weights. In benchmarks, it proved Llama 4 Maverick running at 110 tokens per second on a single H100 GPU.

📊 Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, taking the top spot on Artificial Analysis's AI ranking leaderboard. According to benchmark reports, its primary advancement comes in cybersecurity applications where it identifies system security flaws.

🏫 Google told The New York Times and confirmed in an education update that K-12 student accounts will completely lose access to Google Search, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Gemini in Classroom if their school opts to reject Google's AI features.

⚙️ OpenAI detailed how ChatGPT and Codex are being applied directly to physical world engineering, assisting technical teams with computer-aided design (CAD), PCB design, simulation, and hardware workflows.

As models integrate deeper into education, hardware design, and security benchmarking, verification tools like FlashProve offer a path to validate outputs cryptographically while keeping model weights private.
